column9: Can be used to filter data from: R Analysis GSR Peak Detection
column10: Raw GSR conductance from the GSR sensor.
column11: GSR conductance after linear interpolation for gaps shorter than the threshold.
column12: Slow varying tonic component of GSR conductance.
column13: Fast varying phasic component of GSR conductance.
column14: Binary signal, where GSR samples falling within the onset and offset of the detected GSR peak are assigned a value of 1. Samples outside peaks are assigned a value of 0.
column15: Amplitude of the GSR peak, i.e. the difference between the maximum value of the phasic signal during the peak and its value at the onset.
column16: Binary signal, where the maximum point of each detected GSR peak is assigned a value of 1. Other samples are assigned a value of 0.
column17: Binary signal, where GSR samples obtained by linear interpolation are assigned a value of 1. Other samples that are not obtained by linear interpolation are assigned a value of 0.
